title: Endometriosis non-hormonal disease-modifying treatment
bottleneck: Endometriosis affects roughly 10% of reproductive-age women, causing severe pain and infertility, but diagnosis requires surgery with an average delay of 7 to 10 years, and treatments are hormonal suppression or surgical excision, neither curative, with high recurrence.
why_it_blocks: A common, debilitating disease is managed with blunt tools because its pathogenesis, spanning retrograde menstruation, immune dysfunction, and stem cells, remains disputed.
current_state: Non-hormonal candidates targeting inflammation, angiogenesis, and neurogenesis are in trials, alongside noninvasive diagnostics. No disease-modifying, non-hormonal therapy is approved. The average diagnostic delay of nearly a decade means many patients suffer through their most fertile years without answers. Noninvasive diagnostics based on blood or menstrual-fluid biomarkers could transform care, but none is yet validated for routine use, and research funding lags far behind the disease's prevalence.
